evidence_tier: PILOT (analytic world, rung 1). Mechanism identification only; whatever survives gets a registered confirmation on gated environments. The analytic world's factorized design makes the population secant identity excess = kappa * a EXACT at all magnitudes (H4 absent by construction) and every baseline quadrature-exact, so the measured amplification decomposes into machinery terms: level 1 adds the grid and pseudo-loss charge (H1), level 2 adds calibration noise with quadrature-exact risk evaluation (H2), level 3 adds literal per-test-covariate thresholds (H3). The rung-1 exactness selftest gates the run.
question: Which machinery term owns m(alpha), and which owns the budget-independent plateau above 1 that the Phase 0 budget grid found (m -> 1.106 at alpha 0.10, 1.256 at 0.05 on claims as n_cal grows)?

predictions.P-SW1: Instrument check: m_pop = 1 within 1e-6 at every cell with |a| > 1e-6. The identity is exact here; any deviation is a bug in the instrument, not a finding.
predictions.P-SW2: H1 is a minor, alpha-flat term: |m_grid - 1| <= 0.05 at n_cal >= 1000 at every alpha, and the range of m_grid across alphas at n_cal 1000 is <= 0.05. The grid and B-term shift both arms conservatively and mostly cancel in the paired difference.
predictions.P-SW3: H2 owns the budget-dependent component: m_noise decreases in n_cal at every alpha, increases as alpha falls at fixed n_cal, and at n_cal = 100000 lands within 0.05 of m_grid at every alpha >= 0.05 (the noise term dies with budget; it has no plateau of its own).
predictions.P-SW4: RISKY, the plateau ownership test: the per-covariate gap m_percov - m_noise is positive, persists at n_cal = 100000, and grows as alpha falls: at n_cal >= 10000 the gap is >= 0.10 at alpha 0.05 and >= 0.05 at alpha 0.10. Mechanism: under a positive tilt the per-covariate thresholds rise exactly where the blind-driver conditional wrongness is high, and the oracle's weight spread exceeds the tempered arm's, so per-covariate averaging helps the oracle more, inflating the paired difference multiplicatively.
predictions.P-SW5: Tier tie: the full-machinery m_percov at (alpha 0.10, n_cal 1000) lies in [1.05, 1.35] and at (alpha 0.05, n_cal 1000) in [1.25, 1.75], reproducing the gated-tier m scale inside the analytic world.

falsifiers.P-SW1: Any violation stops the phase until the instrument is fixed.
falsifiers.P-SW2: m_grid carrying an alpha trend > 0.05 means H1 owns part of m(alpha) and the grid-refinement discriminator must run on the gated environments before anything else.
falsifiers.P-SW3: m_noise plateauing above m_grid at 100000 means the noise term itself has a budget-independent floor, which no current mechanism story predicts; loud checkpoint.
falsifiers.P-SW4: A gap under 0.03 at large n_cal kills H3 as the plateau owner. With H4 structurally absent here and H1/H2 measured separately, all four candidates would then be dead for the plateau, which per the handover is the most interesting outcome and goes straight to the human checkpoint, stated loudly.
falsifiers.P-SW5: A pilot-tier m far from the gated-tier scale means the analytic world is missing an ingredient the real environments have, and its mechanism verdicts transfer only qualitatively.

decision_rule: m per level per cell = paired difference at that level divided by (kappa_exact * a_exact), both quadrature-exact. Cell grid: alpha {0.02, 0.05, 0.10, 0.15} x n_cal {250, 1000, 10000, 100000} x gamma {0.0, 0.4, 0.7, 1.3, 1.6} at b = 0.8. Aggregates per (alpha, n_cal) average over gamma cells with |a_exact| > 1e-6. 300 trials (60 at n_cal 100000, where SEs stay adequate because quadrature evaluation removes the evaluation-window noise). Verdicts prediction-by-prediction, misses verbatim.
notes: Registered after the Phase 0 budget verdicts and before any full switchboard run; the P-SW4 gap thresholds are chosen so that the claims plateau (0.10 to 0.26 above 1) would be attributed to H3 only if the analytic world reproduces a same-order gap. No probe of the switchboard levels was run before registration; the smoke run is pipeline debugging only and is labelled pilot in RUNLOG.
